R046-01.notes: Summer job with aunt Rosalind ('The summer I turned sixteen... work in my aunt Rosalind's shop') ending with 'I noticed the signs along the route for the first time... and I found that I could tell.' A is not a how-to; B rivalry is a minor detail; D the narrator did not lose a customer ('Leave it').

R046-02.notes: 'in the tone people use for a relative who has taken up the accordion' signals viewing it as odd/unserious. A contradicts tone; C not supported (she names it 'a sign business'); D no support.

R046-03.notes: Asked 'how many more she wanted', she says 'That depends on the O' -- practice continues until the O is good; later 'By the third week, my O's had stopped sagging. I was promoted.' C is the main trap (literal reading about O shapes) but nothing supports size differences.

flags: minor: near-verbatim lift of 'the gold leaf that the print shop could not imitate'; B/C/D are all print-shop advantages, so very easy
R046-04.notes: 'or when an owner wanted the gold leaf that the print shop could not imitate.' B, C, D describe the print shop ('in an afternoon, in any of four hundred typefaces, for less').

R046-05.notes: 'she studied them the way other people read letters' -- treats photographs of old signs as personal correspondence worth close attention. B 'copy exactly' overreaches; C takes 'letters' literally; D contradicted ('many of them by painters who had died before I was born').

R046-06.notes: 'By the third week, my O's had stopped sagging. I was promoted to the rest of the alphabet and then, in August, to a real job: the name of a hardware store'; bus ride is 'that evening' after. Order C, B, A, D; passage order matches chronology.

R046-07.notes: 'The owner, who had been frowning at the S, seemed to decide that he had been admiring it all along' -- after Rosalind's remark he reframes the flaw as a virtue. A unsupported (narrator noticed first, owner came out later); C no evidence he wanted repainting; D contradicted by 'had been frowning at the S.'

flags: minor: B ('never'), C, D are eliminable quickly; B by absolute wording; preceding clause 'I have since come to doubt that she believed this entirely' nearly states the answer
R046-08.notes: 'I have since come to doubt that she believed this entirely; she scraped her own mistakes off without a second look' -- detail supports that 'Leave it' was partly kindness/insight about customers. B contradicted (she had mistakes to scrape); C unsupported; D contradicted ('Leave it').

flags: minor: the simile 'like water collecting in a footprint' supplies the key word 'collecting' directly
R046-09.notes: 'the paint pooled at the bottom of each stroke like water collecting in a footprint.' A 'shared' is the common-meaning trap.

flags: minor: stem says 'by the end of the summer' though the scene is the evening of the August hardware-store job; acceptable but slightly loose
R046-10.notes: 'I noticed the signs along the route for the first time—which ones had been cut and which had been painted—and I found that I could tell.' A, C, D unsupported.
